excerpts: # feat: Add usage data for Codex (and implement a usage viewer for future providers/models) - Page: GitHub issue - URL: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/673 - State: open - Author: aaditagrawal - Created: 2026-03-09T12:16:23Z - Updated: 2026-03-09T12:22:29Z - Repository: pingdotgg/t3code - Number: #673 - Comments: 1 --- **Purpose**: To view provider limits for plans inline within T3code without relying on external services like CodexBar **Expected UX:** Collapsible usage information on the sidebar ## Suggested Prompt Implement Codex usage display by calling the Codex app-server JSON-RPC method `account/rateLimits/read` against the active Codex session. Treat the session bucket as `rateLimits.primary`. Treat the weekly bucket as `rateLimits.secondary`. Map those buckets into a `quota` / `quotas` response for the UI, including `percentUsed` and `resetDate`. Label the session bucket from `windowDurationMins` like `Session (5 hrs)`, and label the second bucket as `Weekly`. If no active Codex session exists, return `{ provider: "codex" }` with no quota data. Endpoint / method: `account/rateLimits/read` ## Timeline **aaditagrawal** commented on 2026-03-09T12:19:46Z: > The endpoint and data matters more, it could be hidden away as well, but it'd be useful information to have at a glance, especially for lower tiers (like the $20 plan). > > A centralized abstraction link with providers could also be useful if this has to be extended to other providers like GitHub Copilot (which includes native support for usage information in the SDK via `client.rpc.account.getQuota()`), or Cursor.

# Support for cache write tokens in returned response usage

- Page: GitHub issue
- URL: https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/8367
- State: open
- Author: rahulkarajgikar
- Created: 2025-08-29T19:41:09Z
- Updated: 2026-07-02T09:35:19Z
- Repository: vercel/ai
- Number: #8367
- Comments: 7

## Labels

- ai/provider
- provider/anthropic
- provider/gateway
- support
- task-identify-issue-type-done

---

### Description

Some providers like anthropic also charge for cache writes

https://www.anthropic.com/pricing

It would be great for `generateText`, `streamText` ( `LanguageModelV2Usage`) to  include cache write tokens as well so we can accurately compute cost correctly for all models

### AI SDK Version

v5

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

**rahulkarajgikar** commented on 2025-08-29T19:53:06Z:

**smigolsmigol** commented on 2026-03-22T12:29:22Z:

> I built a gateway alternative that handles this. `@f3d1/llmkit-ai-sdk-provider` is an AI SDK v6 custom provider that routes through a proxy tracking all token types: input, output, cache read, cache write. Returns cost in USD on every request.
>
> ```ts
> import { createLLMKit } from '@f3d1/llmkit-ai-sdk-provider';
> const llmkit = createLLMKit({ apiKey: 'llmk_...' });
> const { text } = await generateText({ model: llmkit.chat('claude-sonnet-4-20250514'), prompt: '...' });
> // cost in x-llmkit-cost response header, full breakdown in dashboard
> ```
>
> Cache tokens are priced correctly per provider (Anthropic cache reads at 10% of input rate, cache writes at 125%). The LanguageModelV3 usage object includes `inputTokens.cacheRead` and `inputTokens.cacheWrite`. No need to parse raw provider metadata. Works as a drop-in provider swap, open source.
>
